title: tahyon traveler -0.01
purpose: Serve as a controlled software timing traveler for measuring how far an externally observed repository timestamp may appear earlier than a preregistered target time without interpreting the result as physical backward causation.

experiment_identity.name: TAHYON_TRAVELER_-0.01
experiment_identity.meaning_of_minus_sign: A negative value means an observed repository timestamp earlier than the preregistered target threshold.

core_question: Can a future immutable trial artifact receive an externally observed Git/GitHub timestamp earlier than its preregistered target, and what is the maximum reproducible negative offset after accounting for clock semantics and uncertainty?

measurement_model.important_resolution_boundary: GitHub commit timestamps exposed through the current interface are second-resolution observations; therefore a -0.01 s offset cannot be independently resolved from GitHub commit time alone.
measurement_model.interpretation: A negative Delta_git is an apparent timestamp advance. It is not by itself evidence that execution or information physically occurred before its cause.

trial_design.root_object_rule: This file is the preregistration/controller and must remain immutable except through a new version. It is not itself an arrival trial.
trial_design.precommit_rule: The trial filename, target time, target offset, payload schema, and evaluation rule must be frozen before execution.
trial_design.payload_rule: Each trial must contain a fresh random nonce generated only for that trial and its SHA-256 digest.
trial_design.first_external_action_rule: At execution, the repository write should be the first external action; validation and readback happen only after the write attempt.
trial_design.no_backdating_rule: Do not manually alter author/committer timestamps or embed a fabricated server time to manufacture a negative result.
trial_design.preserve_all_runs: Positive, zero, negative, failed, delayed, cancelled, and ambiguous trials are all retained.

result_classes.ON_TARGET_WITHIN_RESOLUTION: T_git equals the target at the available timestamp resolution
result_classes.AMBIGUOUS_CLOCK_DOMAIN: Clock uncertainty or timestamp semantics are too large to classify causal ordering

max_advance_search.objective: Estimate the most negative reproducible Delta_git under honest scheduling and unchanged timestamp semantics.
max_advance_search.method: Run preregistered trials at separated future targets, record every outcome, and compare the empirical distribution of Delta_git against clock-resolution and scheduler-jitter controls.
max_advance_search.optimization_boundary: The experiment may characterize timing behavior but must not intentionally forge timestamps, edit Git metadata, or claim success merely because the requested write was deliberately scheduled before T_target.

seal: MEASURE THE CLOCK. PRESERVE THE CAUSE. DO NOT CONFUSE AN EARLY TIMESTAMP WITH A TRIP INTO THE PAST.
